actions.description: What the detail allows. `provenance` is an action only alongside `read` (HCP 6.1.5, 7.4.1); not checked by the schema.

narrowedTo.description: An implementation-defined narrowing below category grain, which only narrows (HCP 6.1.5.1). To a Context Client, entries it names are named by `ref`, never by `id` (HCP 5.2.6).

onwardSharing.description: The onward sharing the person elected for the detail (HCP 3.12, 6.1.5).

purposes.description: The purposes the person approved for these categories; never empty (HCP 6.1.5.2).

AccessRequest.description: One HCP authorization detail as requested (HCP 6.1.5, 13.3).

actions.description: HCP `actions`: what the client may do with the categories. `provenance` only alongside `read` (HCP 6.1.5, 7.4.1).

categories.description: HCP `categories` the detail covers (HCP 4.5, 6.1.5). The maxItems of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

narrowedTo.description: HCP `narrowedTo` (HCP 6.1.5.1): implementation-defined keys that only narrow. A key the provider does not support is refused with malformedRequest (HCP 6.1.5.1 rule 2).

onwardSharing.description: HCP `onwardSharing` (HCP 3.12, 6.1.4, 6.1.5): asks that the person be offered onward sharing for this detail, as a separate act after they confirm the grant. delegation.description: The delegation under which a delegate authorized the grant; present only then (HCP 6.1.5, 17.4).

Category.description: An HCP context category (HCP 4.5), the primary unit of access control: either a slug from HCP's category registry, such as `general_preferences` or `health_context`, or a custom category written as an absolute URI under a domain its definer controls. Grant.description: A grant (HCP 6.1.5). `expiresAt` is an instant for a `temporary` grant and null for a `persistent` one (HCP 6.1.4, 6.1.5). NextStepHint.description: The `hint` a provider puts in the `trust-task-next-step` entry that holds a request (the entry whose `typeUri` is this specification's request Type URI). trust-task-next-step leaves a hint's shape to the specification its `typeUri` names, and a client validates the hint against this definition, addressed by its anchor (`https://trusttasks.org/spec/hcp/grants/request/0.1#next-step-hint`), before it uses it; a hint that fails is ignored, as if absent. retryAfter.description: How long the client should wait before it resubmits, as a whole number of seconds counted from receipt of the next step; the client SHOULD NOT resubmit sooner. notTo.description: Set by the provider: each DNS domain or operator a standing rule denies any of the detail's categories (HCP 6.1.5, 6.3).

name.description: HCP `requestingParty.name`: a name the person can recognize, shown before they act (HCP 6.1.6). The maxLength, the same as the stored grant's `requestingParty.name`, is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Purpose.description: A purpose with a description the person can read (HCP 6.1.5.2).

description.description: The description shown to the person before approval (HCP 6.1.5.2, 6.1.6).

PurposeCode.description: An HCP purpose code: an absolute URI naming the purpose for which context is requested or may be used (HCP 6.1.5.2).

RequestedPurpose.description: An HCP purpose (HCP 6.1.5.2): a code and a description the person can read.

REQUIRED: HCP's purpose carries the description shown to the person before they approve (HCP 6.1.5.2), so a requested purpose always has one. type.description: A person or an organization. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

Response.description: The person approved: the access token issued under the grant, as HCP's OAuth token response carries it (HCP 13.3, 13.4), and the grant as approved, as HCP's grant object (HCP 6.1.5). accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the new grant (the token response's `access_token`, HCP 13.3), opaque to the client. Response.title: HCP — Request Grant — response payload

Uri.description: An absolute URI with no whitespace, as HCP writes every custom value at an extension point (HCP A.3).

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

schema.description: A Context Client asks an HCP Provider for a grant over a person's context, naming what it needs as HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5; RFC 9396 `authorization_details` of the HCP type, as HCP 13.3 names them). HCP Core defines no grant-request operation (HCP 6.1.7 leaves it to the profiles), so this task carries no HCP operation: it is a Trust-Task-native authenticated channel in the sense of HCP 6.1.6 and 12.2. The person decides out of band; while they do, the provider answers with trust-task-next-step. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

access.description: What the client asks to be granted: one or more HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5 `access`, HCP 13.3). The provider shows each to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6). The maxItems of 16 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

expiresIn.description: For a temporary grant, the lifetime the client asks for, in seconds. Absent means HCP's default of 4 hours; HCP's maximum is 24 hours (HCP 6.1.3). The provider MAY grant less and never more. Ignored for a persistent grant.

grantType.description: The kind of grant the client asks for (HCP 6.1.4). Absent means `temporary`, HCP's default. `persistent` only lets the person be offered persistence as a separate affirmative act; it never pre-selects it (HCP 6.1.4), and the grant is temporary unless the person elects otherwise. Pending HCP confirmation (question 24).

requestingParty.description: HCP `requestingParty` (HCP 3.4, 6.1.5): the person or organization on whose behalf the client asks, where it differs from the Context Subject. Shown to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6).

subjectHint.description: An identifier by which the provider can find the person whose context is asked for, and reach them to decide — the counterpart of OpenID Connect `login_hint`. Absent where the provider serves one person only. The provider never says whether it knows the hint (see the specification's Errors). Pending HCP confirmation (question 23).
